A painted bird's-eye map of Eyrland, a great river basin like a tilted bowl: grey mountains with steaming springs on the north rim, a dark old forest in the west, rolling hills and sheep country to the east, and the sea along the bottom. The Tamber River runs north to south through the middle, widening into a huge mirror-smooth lake two-thirds of the way up (the Glasswater), with a reed marsh south of the lake, then down past a walled capital to a port city at the river's mouth. Emberford sits on islands where the river splits. Small cold lake in the foothills; a tributary out of the western forest; another out of the eastern hills. A dead-calm patch of sea far to the south. Only what a local would know.  Keep key features well spaced so the DM can crop sections.
